title: HP Hampden X3027 - Relics
memorial_details: A propeller, undercarriage leg and tyre from Hampden X3027 with associated display board and laminated information sheets. The propellor was discovered, and then recovered from the crash site on 28/9/1992 and was subsequently put on display, along with a brass commemorative plaque (see wmr 109504) in the Skegness RNLI Boat shed. In February 2017 a larger vessel was delivered and due to restricted space the propeller was donated to the Lincolnshire Aviation Heritage Centre at East Kirkby. It is now displayed here, along with one of the main undercarriage struts and a tyre which were also recovered from the crash site. Further items recovered from the aircraft are held in storage at East Kirkby
inscription: Partial transcription from the display sheets: Propeller from Handley Page Hampden X3027/ On the night of the 27/28 October 1940;/ RAF Bomber Command tasked/ 82 aircraft across numerous targets in Germany and the Occupied/ Countries. At RAF Scampton, between 15:00 and 17:40 hrs 49 Squadron/ dispatched 8 Hampdens with 6 aircraft hitting the primary target of/ Hamburg and the remaining 2 bombing alternative targets. Squadron/ losses were limited to 1 damaged (X3001) and 1 shot down (X3027)/ Hampden X3001 (Pilot Officer Green and crew.) successfully located/ and bombed their allocated target but on return to Lincolnshire and/ whilst orbiting RAF Scampton's Q Site (the decoy flarepath at Rand) was/ attacked by a nightfighter of 2/NJG2 flown by Leutnant Heinz Völker./ The Hampden suffered slight(!) damage including 3 burst tyres and shot/ accumulators, but landed safely at 01:25 hrs./ It is reported that Hampden X3027, with one engine out of action, was/ heard to circle Skegness before, it is believed, attempting to ditch in the/ sea in shallow water close to shore./ At 02:00 hrs the Lifeboat Hon. Secretary, Mr H E Sparrow, received a/ telephone message from the Skegness Coastguard that an aircraft was/ down just North of the pier and that cries for help could clearly be/ heard. [Partial transcript form the information sheets on the associated display board].
